title: Silent dispatch on a word seam
statement: Let $M$ be a deterministic Turing machine with $k$ work tapes over the Boolean alphabet, and let $q,r$ be states such that, for every input symbol and every tuple of work-tape symbols, the transition from $q$ is the action that leaves the input head and every work head stationary, writes nothing, emits no output, and enters $r$. For every Boolean input word $w$ and every family of words assigned to the $k$ work tapes, one step from the seam configuration in state $q$ yields the seam configuration in state $r$ with the same tape words.
hypotheses_covered: M is a k-work-tape Boolean-alphabet machine
q and r are states of M
for every input and work-tape reading, M transitions from q by a stationary, silent, no-write action to r
w is a Boolean input word
words is an arbitrary family of k Boolean tape words
replaced:
If a control state's transition is the unconditional silent dispatch to a
state $r$, then one step from the canonical word-seam configuration in that
state yields the canonical word-seam configuration in state $r$ with every
other component unchanged.
